### What’s happening
- Supabase sends a recovery link to your site with tokens in the hash (after #).
- Your app wasn’t routing that recovery link to a password reset screen, so the link “opens the app” but doesn’t show a reset form.

### What I implemented
- Added a full reset flow that works in dev and prod.

Changes:
- New route `/reset-password` with `src/pages/AuthPages/ResetPassword.tsx` that updates the user password using Supabase.
- New “Forgot password” page at `/auth/forgot` to send reset emails using `supabase.auth.resetPasswordForEmail`.
- Added an `AuthUrlRouter` that watches the URL; if a Supabase recovery link is opened (hash contains `type=recovery`), it redirects to `/reset-password` so the user immediately sees the form and Supabase can read tokens.
- Added a “Forgot your password?” link to the Sign-in page.

How the redirect works:
- Supabase tokens remain in the location hash; navigating to `/reset-password` doesn’t remove the hash, so `supabase-js` can still detect the recovery session.

### One required Supabase setting
In Supabase Dashboard:
- Go to Authentication → URL Configuration → Site URL
- Set it to your app URL, e.g. for dev: `http://localhost:5273`
- In Email Templates → Reset password, ensure the “Redirect URL” is either empty (uses Site URL) or explicitly set to `http://localhost:5273/reset-password`

Note: If your dev server sometimes runs on a different port, update Site URL accordingly. Our code already does `redirectTo: ${window.location.origin}/reset-password` for the email, so using the app’s current origin is supported.

### How to test
1. Start the app on your dev port (5273).
2. Go to `/auth/forgot`, enter the user’s email.
3. Open the email and click the link. It should open your app, auto-redirect to `/reset-password`, and show the form.
4. Enter the new password; you’ll be redirected to Sign-in.

### Summary
- Added `ResetPassword` and `ForgotPassword` pages and wired routes in `src/App.tsx`.
- Implemented `AuthUrlRouter` and included it in `src/main.tsx` to auto-redirect recovery links to `/reset-password`.
- Updated `SignInForm` to link to `/auth/forgot`.
- No linter issues introduced.
- Set Supabase “Site URL” and optional “Redirect URL” so emails link to `http://localhost:5273/reset-password` (or your prod domain).

### SQL to add `profiles.role_id` FK and assign admin to three users

Run this in Supabase SQL editor.

- Add `role_id` column, FK, and index (idempotent)
```sql
-- 1) Add column if missing
do $$
begin
  if not exists (
    select 1
    from information_schema.columns
    where table_schema = 'public'
      and table_name = 'profiles'
      and column_name = 'role_id'
  ) then
    alter table public.profiles add column role_id uuid;
  end if;
end $$;

-- 2) Add FK constraint to roles(id) if missing
do $$
begin
  if not exists (
    select 1
    from pg_constraint c
    join pg_class t on c.conrelid = t.oid
    join pg_namespace n on n.oid = t.relnamespace
    where n.nspname = 'public'
      and t.relname = 'profiles'
      and c.conname = 'profiles_role_id_fkey'
  ) then
    alter table public.profiles
      add constraint profiles_role_id_fkey
      foreign key (role_id)
      references public.roles(id)
      on update cascade
      on delete set null;
  end if;
end $$;

-- 3) Helpful index
create index if not exists profiles_role_id_idx on public.profiles(role_id);
```

- Ensure there is an `admin` role (safe if it already exists)
```sql
insert into public.roles (id, name)
select gen_random_uuid(), 'admin'
where not exists (
  select 1 from public.roles where lower(name) = 'admin'
);
```

- Assign the `admin` role to exactly three users by email
Replace the emails with your three admins’ emails. This assumes `profiles.email` is populated (your code inserts it on sign-up).

```sql
-- Set admin for three users by email
update public.profiles p
set role_id = r.id
from public.roles r
where lower(r.name) = 'admin'
  and p.email in (
    'first.admin@example.com',
    'second.admin@example.com',
    'third.admin@example.com'
  );
```

- Optional: verify assignment
```sql
select p.id, p.email, p.role_id, r.name as role_name
from public.profiles p
left join public.roles r on r.id = p.role_id
where p.email in (
  'first.admin@example.com',
  'second.admin@example.com',
  'third.admin@example.com'
);
```

If your `profiles` table does not include an `email` column, use `auth.users` linkage instead:
```sql
-- Example: map by user ids instead of emails
update public.profiles p
set role_id = r.id
from public.roles r
where lower(r.name) = 'admin'
  and p.id in (
    'uuid-of-user-1',
    'uuid-of-user-2',
    'uuid-of-user-3'
  );
```

- Optional: choose a default role for new users (if desired)
```sql
-- Choose your default role name here, e.g., 'user'
update public.profiles p
set role_id = r.id
from public.roles r
where p.role_id is null
  and lower(r.name) = 'user';
```

- RLS note: No change required if your existing `profiles` select policy already allows reading own profile. Role updates should be restricted to admins or service role.

- Frontend note: Your app already reads `profiles`; once `role_id` is populated, your role-based gating will work consistently.

- If you want, share the 3 admin emails and I’ll tailor the exact UPDATE for you.

- I can also add this migration as a new SQL file in `Database Schema Creation SQL Scripts` on request.

- Short summary
  - Added FK `profiles.role_id -> roles.id` safely.
  - Verified/created `admin` role.
  - Provided UPDATE to set three users to admin by email.

Status: I updated the All Users screen to persist role changes via the new FK and to display the role name via a join. The remaining blockers are Supabase Auth settings (signups disabled) and RLS on `profiles` preventing admins from updating others.

Do these two fixes:

1) Allow user creation
- Fastest: enable email signups
  - Supabase Dashboard → Authentication → Providers → Email
  - Turn OFF “Disable new user signups” (i.e., allow signups)
  - Then creating a user from All Users will work again using the existing signUp flow
- Recommended (no global signups): admin provisioning via server
  - Create a secure server endpoint or an Edge Function that calls `supabase.auth.admin.createUser` or `inviteUserByEmail` using the service role key
  - Change the All Users “Add User” flow to call this endpoint (we can add this for you if you prefer; you’ll need to provide the function deploy or server environment)

2) Let admins update any profile (RLS)
Run this SQL in Supabase to grant admin users update/select on all profiles. It checks the signed-in user’s `profiles.role_id` against `roles.name = 'admin'`.

```sql
-- Ensure RLS enabled
alter table public.profiles enable row level security;

-- Helper condition: is current user an admin?
-- Used inline in policies via EXISTS subquery.

-- Select: allow user to read own profile or admins to read all
do $$
begin
  if not exists (
    select 1 from pg_policies where schemaname='public' and tablename='profiles' and policyname='profiles_select_own_or_admin'
  ) then
    create policy profiles_select_own_or_admin
    on public.profiles
    for select
    to authenticated
    using (
      auth.uid() = id
      or exists (
        select 1
        from public.profiles p
        join public.roles r on r.id = p.role_id
        where p.id = auth.uid() and lower(r.name) = 'admin'
      )
    );
  end if;
end $$;

-- Update: allow user to update own profile or admins to update any
do $$
begin
  if not exists (
    select 1 from pg_policies where schemaname='public' and tablename='profiles' and policyname='profiles_update_own_or_admin'
  ) then
    create policy profiles_update_own_or_admin
    on public.profiles
    for update
    to authenticated
    using (
      auth.uid() = id
      or exists (
        select 1
        from public.profiles p
        join public.roles r on r.id = p.role_id
        where p.id = auth.uid() and lower(r.name) = 'admin'
      )
    )
    with check (true);
  end if;
end $$;

-- Insert (optional): allow only admins to insert profiles, needed if admins create users
do $$
begin
  if not exists (
    select 1 from pg_policies where schemaname='public' and tablename='profiles' and policyname='profiles_insert_admin_only'
  ) then
    create policy profiles_insert_admin_only
    on public.profiles
    for insert
    to authenticated
    with check (
      exists (
        select 1
        from public.profiles p
        join public.roles r on r.id = p.role_id
        where p.id = auth.uid() and lower(r.name) = 'admin'
      )
    );
  end if;
end $$;
```
